transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

U on your Beko means: Pan not detected / unsuitable cookware (display shows U on induction models). This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Induction zones only heat magnetic pans of the right size. A flashing pan symbol (often 'U' or a pan icon) means no suitable pan is detected. A magnet sticking firmly to the pan base shows it is induction-compatible. It would be worth a closer look if a known induction-compatible pan of the right size is not detected on any zone. Now try switching a zone on. Is it working now, or still not?
Still not working! I tried my saucepan again and it just flashes the U and doesn't heat. Is the hob definitely faulty?

It is not definitely faulty, as a "U" code often indicates an external issue like incompatible cookware or a power supply problem rather than a broken appliance. Since it is brand new and newly fitted, you should check if the saucepan base is flat and magnetic before assuming the hob itself is defective. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the pan not suiting induction. Many hobs have a key / child lock (often a key or padlock symbol) that stops the zones coming on — the manual shows which button to hold. Was the lock on (and is it off now), or was there no lock on?
I don't think the child lock was on, the other buttons work fine. So what else could it be? I've only got this one problem since it was fitted 2 days ago!

It depends on whether the hob is induction or ceramic, as a "U" code typically indicates an issue with the cookware or sensor. You should check if you are using compatible pans and ensure they are centered correctly on the heating zone. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Induction zones only heat magnetic pans of the right size. A flashing pan symbol (often 'U' or a pan icon) means no suitable pan is detected. A magnet sticking firmly to the pan base shows it is induction-compatible. It would be worth a closer look if a known induction-compatible pan of the right size is not detected on any zone. Check the hob's isolator switch (often a large switch on the wall or in a cupboard) is on, and look at the fuse box for a breaker that has switched off. If a breaker keeps tripping, don't keep resetting it. Was the isolator or a breaker off (and is it sorted), or were they all on?
I haven't touched the isolator or the fuse box, but the hob has power because the controls all light up and respond! It's only the zone that flashes the U. What else could it be?

It depends on whether the hob is induction or ceramic, as a "U" code typically indicates an issue with the sensor or control board. Since you have already tried different pans and confirmed the controls respond, the fault likely lies within the internal electronics rather than user error. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

It flashes the U every time I use my usual pans since it was fitted, no other codes. The only thing that has heated is my cast-iron casserole, but my aluminium saucepans and a copper-bottomed pan don't. Does that help?
Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

I literally just told you! It flashes a U every time with my usual pans, and nothing else happens. No other codes, no noises or smells. The cast-iron casserole is the only thing that's heated. What do you think is wrong?

The "U" code indicates an incompatible pan detection issue, which is normal for induction hobs. It means your usual pans are not magnetic enough to work with the appliance. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?
